yes.0: Thank you! My wife likes many flowers, but #b#t4031025##k is her favorite. Go to #m105040300# and click #p1061006# to find them.
yes.1: Please get me #b10 #t4031025#s#k. I think 10 will cover the house with that pleasant scent. Please hurry!

no.0: I understand... my wedding anniversary is coming up and I am screwed! Please come back if you have some spare time.

1.0: Ohhh... you got me #b10 #b#t4031025#s#k! This is awesome... I can't believe you went deep into the forest and got these flowers... there's a story about this flower where it supposedly doesn't die for 100 years. With this, I can make my wife happy.
1.1: Oh, and since you have worked hard for me, I should reward you well. I found some #t4003000#s in the ship. Some travelers leave things here and there. It looks like something you may need, so take it.

yes.0: If you have time, why not try going back into the forest? You may find an important item in there. I can't guarantee it since obviously I've never been there before, so please don't come back complaining if all you can find is trash.

item.0: You haven't gotten #b#t4031025##k yet. There's #p1061006# at #m105040300# and I heard that with that you can go to the place where #t4031025##k is. Please go into the forest and collect #t4031025##k for me. I need 10 to make my wedding anniversary

QuestInfo.name: [Forest of Tenacity] John's Pink Flower Basket
QuestInfo.0: Talk to John in either Sleepywood or Lith Harbor.
QuestInfo.1: You met John the fisherman. He wants to give his wife a flower basket for their wedding anniversary. He assumed you would bring him #b10 Pink Violas#k for some reason. John says you can use the Mysterious Statue in Sleepywood to go to where the flowers are.\n\n#i4031025# #t4031025# #b#c4031025#/10#k
QuestInfo.2: I got John all #b10 Pink Violas#k. With these, he can make a beautiful flower basket for his wife on their anniversary. As a sign of appreciation, John got me a whole bunch of screws left over from ships here and there. By the way, if there are this many screws that have fallen out of ships, then how in the world are they even working...? Are they carrying passengers on it?
